parole.significato: a married or divorced woman or a widow
parole.testo: From Old Hungarian achscin, axsin, from Alanic *æxšiññæ.

parole.significato: whole, entire, complete (with all parts included, with nothing missing)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Alanic *ægaš (“undiminished, whole”). Compare Ossetian ӕга́с (ægás, “whole”).
First attested in 1372. From Alanic *ɣaždug. Compare Ossetian хъӕзды́г (qæzdýg), гъӕздуг (ǧæzdug, “rich”). The noun gazda probably influenced the voicing of the word-initial consonant.
From Alanic; compare Ossetian лӕг (læg, “man, male”).
From Old Hungarian ruoz (*ruosz) or ruvoz (*ruvosz), from *rowasə, borrowed from Alanic *roβas (“fox”) (compare Ossetian рувас (ruvas), робас (robas)). Doublet of róka.

Inherited from Old Hungarian *reðə, possibly borrowed from Alanic *roδ, perhaps via a Northwest Caucasian or Northeast Caucasian language because of the vocalism of the Alanic reconstruction, ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawdʰás.

parole.significato: cheese (a dairy product made from curdled or cultured milk)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Alanic *ciɣd. Compare Ossetian цыхт (cyxt, “cheese”).

parole.significato: armor, armour (a protective layer over a body intended to deflect damaging forces)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Alanic, compare Ossetian уарт (wart, “shield”).

parole.significato: green (having a color between yellow and blue)
parole.testo: From Old Hungarian zeld, of uncertain further origin. Most likely borrowed from Alanic *zæld, from Proto-Iranian *járHitah (“yellow”). Compare Ossetian зӕлдӕ (zældæ, “a kind of grass”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃- (“yellow”).

Of unknown origin according to Zaicz. Some, e.g. Róna-Tas and Berta, support Munkácsi's etymology as a loan from Alanic *iδæǰ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *HwidʰáwaH (modern Ossetian идӕдз (idæʒ)), with the same development of *wi- as in öl.
Borrowed from Alanic *aβəgæ. First attested in 1359.

Of debated origin. Either: # Borrowed from Alanic. Compare Ossetian марг (marg, “poison”). Further akin to Persian مرگ (marg, “death”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *mirkkɜ (“poison”). Compare Finnish myrkky (“poison”), but this is problematic.

parole.significato: guest (a recipient of hospitality, specifically someone staying by invitation at the house of another)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Alanic *βændæg (“hostage, guest”). Alternatively, borrowed from Old Italian venedigo, venetico (“Venetian”).
